thesis: SanDisk, spun off from Western Digital in February 2026, is a pure-play NAND flash memory leader serving enterprise SSD, client, and consumer storage markets. Q4 FY2026 delivered record revenue of $8.97B with non-GAAP EPS of $39.25 (beat by 13%), driven by AI-fueled enterprise SSD demand and NAND pricing recovery. TTM revenue stands at ~$20.3B with strong margins. However, the stock has been volatile since spinoff — trading from ~$38 post-separation to a 52-week high of $2,354 before pulling back to ~$1,485. The cyclical NAND market, capital intensity, and potential oversupply remain risks. HOLD at current levels; accumulate on pullbacks toward $1,100–1,200.

drivers: Enterprise SSD demand from AI training and inference workloads sustains multi-year growth
NAND pricing power continues as supply discipline holds and demand outstrips capacity
Pure-play flash story attracts dedicated semiconductor investors post-spinoff
Next-gen QLC and high-layer 3D NAND technology transitions improve cost per bit

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows 15–25% YoY as NAND pricing stabilizes at healthy levels, enterprise SSD mix stays elevated, and EPS reaches ~$120–140 annualized. Market applies a 12–14x forward P/E appropriate for a cyclical memory company near peak margins.

risks: NAND oversupply cycle re-emerges as Samsung, SK hynix, and Kioxia expand capacity
NAND ASP declines accelerate, compressing margins from peak levels
Enterprise SSD demand normalizes after the initial AI infrastructure buildout
Post-spinoff execution risks and capital allocation missteps

catalysts.event: Q4 FY2026 results — record revenue $8.97B, non-GAAP EPS $39.25
Q1 FY2027 earnings — post-spinoff capital allocation and NAND pricing outlook
Next-gen enterprise SSD qualifications at hyperscalers for AI workloads

key_risks: NAND flash is deeply cyclical; current elevated margins may represent a near-peak
Newly independent company — limited track record as a standalone public entity
Intense competition from Samsung, SK hynix/Solidigm, and Kioxia
Capital intensity of NAND manufacturing requires heavy ongoing investment
Post-spinoff stock price volatility and limited institutional ownership history
